Parameter domain and the boundary  $p=t$ The parameters are
$$t\geq2,\qquad p\geq\max(t,6),\qquad
t\mid 3p,\qquad k\geq1.$$
Write
$$q=\frac{3p}{t}\in\mathbb Z_{>0}.$$
For each connector, its omitted neighbours among the three relevant families of selected vertices have residues
$$0,1,\ldots,3p-1\pmod t.$$
Every residue occurs exactly  $q$  times. Consequently its degree is
$$\Delta=4p-\frac{3p}{t}
      =\frac{(4t-3)p}{t}.$$
The other degrees are:Vertex typeDegree in completed graph $c,x,y$  $t+1$  $i$  $t+1$ Witness  $a,b$  $p+1$ Connector $(4t-3)p/t$ The connector degree is integral precisely because of the divisibility condition.Also,
$$\Delta\geq p+1\geq t+1.$$
Thus the exact minimum and maximum degrees are indeed
$$\boxed{\delta=t+1,\qquad
\Delta=\frac{(4t-3)p}{t}.}$$
The important boundary  $p=t$ Here
$$\Delta=4t-3.$$
Every connector has degree  $4t-3$ , every witness has degree  $t+1$ , and the selected vertices have degree  $t+1$ .In the intermediate deleted-edge graph  $F^-$ , the two ports have degree  $p=t$ , not  $t+1$ . This is correctly acknowledged in the source. It is not a contradiction: the minimum-degree assertion is made for the completed graph, where the cyclic linking restores one edge to each port.Therefore the boundary case does not rely on an incorrect minimum-degree assertion for the intermediate piece.2. The universal dissociation capThis is the central mathematical question.Let  $D$  be an arbitrary dissociation set of  $F^-$ . Put
$$m=q_A+q_B,$$
where  $q_A,q_B$  count its chosen connectors of the two colours.The essential constraint is correctly applied: each chosen connector has at most one chosen neighbour across its entire physical neighbourhood.In particular, removing the chosen neighbours of several connectors costs at most the number of connectors, not that number multiplied by the number of blocks. Shared neighbours are counted once.The witness kernel gives
$$\#\{\text{chosen witnesses}\}\leq 2p,$$
because each of the  $p$  slots is a  $K_{2,2}$ , and a dissociation set contains at most two vertices from each slot.I checked the connector cases separately.Case A:  $m=0$ The no-connector witness argument gives
$$g_L+g_R\leq p.$$
Each block contributes at most three ordinary vertices plus its good-block indicator. Hence
$$|D|\leq 6p+g_L+g_R\leq7p.$$
This is the correct application of the witness-kernel result.Case B:  $m=1$ Suppose the selected connector is  $A_s$ .There are two possibilities.B1. The connector meets a left  $y$ .Retain only its edges to all left isolates  $i$  and one such  $y_j$ .The resulting comparison graph is precisely the single-unused-vertex configuration covered by the earlier witness-kernel argument, after a cyclic shift of block indices.The shift is legitimate because the fixed kernel used in that argument excludes all offset-zero  $b$ -to- $b$  edges. It does not depend on which one of those edges was physically deleted.Adding the actual connector edges back can only decrease the dissociation number.Therefore
$$|D|\leq7p.$$
B2. The connector meets no left  $y$ .This is the previously delicate case.Since  $A_s$  has no edges to any left  $y$ , every left  $y_j$  omits  $A_s$ . The  $x$ - and  $y$ -omissions differ in every block. Thus  $A_s$  meets every left  $x_j$ , as well as every left  $i_j$ .Remove its at most one chosen neighbour.Now all left  $x$ 's and  $i$ 's are absent from the remaining dissociation set.Each left block has only
$$a,\ c,\ y,\ b$$
remaining, with induced structure
$$a\ \sqcup\ (c-y-b).$$
Its contribution is at most
$$2+[a\text{ chosen}].$$
Let  $a_L$  count chosen left  $a$ -witnesses, and let  $g_R$  count good right blocks.The required inequality is
$$\boxed{a_L+g_R\leq p.}$$
Here is the important combinatorial justification.Use slots
$$P_j=(L_j,R_{j+1}).$$
A slot counted twice contains a chosen left  $a$  and a good right block.The complete  $K_{2,2}$  adjacency and dissociation condition force its chosen witnesses to be exactly the two  $a$ -witnesses. The two selected witnesses cross-saturate each other.The surviving predecessor relations then exclude every witness in the preceding slot
$$P_{j-1}=(L_{j-1},R_j).$$
Thus every double-counted slot injects into a distinct slot with neither indicator counted.If  $d_2,d_0$  denote the numbers of double and zero slots, respectively, then
$$d_2\leq d_0.$$
Since there are  $p$  slots,
$$a_L+g_R=p+d_2-d_0\leq p.$$
Consequently the remaining block contribution is bounded by
$$2p+a_L+3p+g_R\leq6p.$$
Restore the removed neighbour and the chosen connector:
$$\boxed{|D|\leq6p+2\leq7p.}$$

$$|D|\leq6p+2+m\leq6p+6\leq7p.$$
Only one connector colour occurs.Choose two distinct connectors of that colour.For two  $A$ 's, their combined neighbourhood forces all left  $x,y,i$  and all right  $c$  absent after removing at most two chosen neighbours.The remaining selected block types contribute at most  $4p$ , and witnesses contribute at most  $2p$ .Thus
$$|D|\leq6p+2+m\leq7p.$$
The  $B$ -only case is the reverse orientation.Both arguments correctly handle shared removed neighbours.Case D:  $m\geq5$ At least three chosen connectors have the same colour.Suppose they are  $A$ -connectors.Every left  $x,y,i$  and every right  $c$  has at least two neighbours among those three chosen connectors. None can belong to a dissociation set.If  $q_B=0$ , the remaining block types contribute at most  $4p$ , witnesses at most  $2p$ , and connectors at most  $m\leq t\leq p$ . Hence
$$|D|\leq7p.$$
If  $q_B\geq1$ , choose one  $B$  and remove its at most one chosen neighbour.All right isolates and at least one right leaf per block are then absent.The remaining selected vertices contribute at most  $2p$ , witnesses at most  $2p$ , the removed neighbour at most one, and all connectors at most  $m\leq2t$ .Thus
$$|D|\leq4p+1+2t
\leq6p+1
\leq7p.$$
The case with at least three  $B$ 's is symmetric in the counting sense, with the reverse orientation handled explicitly.This completes the arbitrary-dissociation-set argument.3. Exact attainment of the capThe proposed  $7p$ -vertex set isleft blocks:  $c,x,i$ ;right blocks:  $x,y,a,b$ ;no connectors.Its induced edges are exactly:left  $c-x$ ;right  $x-a$ ;right  $y-b$ .All other selected vertices are isolated.There are no selected cross-witness edges because the left witnesses are absent.Therefore it is a dissociation set of size  $7p$ , both before and after deletion of  $e$ .Together with the universal cap,
$$\boxed{\beta_2(F^-)=\beta_2(F)=7p.}$$
This is an actual combinatorial equality proof, not an inference from finite model optima.4. Two-connectivityI independently checked the spanning-subgraph argument.Step 1: Witness cycleThe witness edges of offsets two and three produce the cycle
$$L_s-R_{s+3}-L_{s+1},$$
with indices modulo  $2p$ .Both offsets exist in the baseline interface because
$$p-2\geq4$$
for the stipulated  $p\geq6$ .The cycle visits every left and right witness exactly once. It avoids the deleted offset-zero edge  $e$ .Thus it is a Hamiltonian cycle on the witness vertices.Step 2: Add block pathsFor each block, add the ear
$$a-x-c-y-b.$$
Its endpoints are distinct vertices already on the cycle. Adding an open ear between distinct vertices of a 2-connected graph preserves 2-connectivity.This adds all  $x,c,y$ .Step 3: Add connectorsEach connector has at least  $p$  old neighbours among the  $x,y$  vertices of its own wing.Indeed, the two omissions differ in each block, so at least one of  $x_j,y_j$  is adjacent to any fixed connector.Since  $p\geq6$ , each connector can be adjoined with at least two distinct existing neighbours.Step 4: Add isolatesEach  $i_j$  has its old neighbour  $b_j$  and all  $t\geq2$  connectors of its colour.It can therefore be added with at least two distinct old neighbours.All vertices have now been included in a 2-connected spanning subgraph of  $F^-$ .Hence
$$\boxed{F^-\text{ is 2-connected}.}$$
This argument works without any minimum-degree assumption on  $F^-$  beyond what the actual construction supplies. In particular, it remains valid at  $p=t$ , where its port degree is only  $t$ .5. Cyclic composition for every  $k$ Take  $k$  copies of  $F^-$  and connect successive pieces using their distinct left and right ports.For  $k=1$ , the additional edge restores  $e$ , giving  $F$ .For  $k\geq2$ , consider deletion of any vertex.Its own piece remains connected by 2-connectivity.At most one external linking edge is destroyed, since the entry and exit ports are distinct.The cyclic sequence of pieces remains connected.At  $k=2$ , there are two distinct links between the pieces, and deletion of one port destroys at most one of them. The other survives.Therefore the completed graph is two-connected for every  $k\geq1$ .For the dissociation number, restriction to each piece gives
$$\beta_2(G)\leq7pk.$$
Repeating the  $7p$ -vertex attaining set in every piece attains this bound because it excludes the left port of every piece.Consequently,
$$\boxed{\beta_2(G)=7pk.}$$
The composition preserves simplicity, bipartiteness, all physical degrees and the literal one-deletion minimality witnesses.6. Final numerical identityThe resulting parameters are
$$n=(12p+2t)k,\qquad
|S|=8pk,\qquad
\beta_2(G)=7pk.$$
Therefore
$$d=|S|-\beta_2(G)=pk.$$
Substitute
$$\delta=t+1,\qquad
\Delta=\frac{(4t-3)p}{t}.$$
Since
$$8\delta-14=2(4t-3),$$
we obtain
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{\Delta n}{12\Delta+8\delta-14}
&=
\frac{
\frac{(4t-3)p}{t}(12p+2t)k
}{
\frac{12(4t-3)p}{t}+2(4t-3)
}\\
&=pk\\
&=d.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus the proposed equality is exact throughout the full parameter domain.7. None of the witness relations used in the proof requires an offset-zero  $b$ – $b$  edge. Consequently every cyclic translate of those relations survives the same deletion  $b_0^L b_0^R$ . In a slot counted twice by the good/good, chosen- $a$ /good, or good/chosen- $a$  count, the chosen witnesses must be precisely the two  $a$ 's. They saturate each other and exclude both witnesses in each block of the predecessor slot. The predecessor map is injective. This proves all three inequalities
$$g_L+g_R\le p,\qquad a_L+g_R\le p,\qquad g_L+a_R\le p$$

With  $r$  good blocks in the opposite wing, that wing contributes at most  $3p+r$ .
